Content: About `40%` of the world's population lives within `100` `text(kilometers)` of a coastal area. A student is asked to identify and explain which type of renewable energy resource is most appropriate for these areas.
Which information `text(best)` completes the student's assignment?

A.Choice: Floating solar panels are most appropriate because coastal areas are cloudy and offshore waves are always calm.

B.Choice: Fossil fuels are most appropriate because coastal winds will prevent the accumulation of pollution along coastal areas.

C.Choice: Nuclear energy is most appropriate because seawater is readily available in coastal areas and can be used to cool the nuclear reactors.

D.Choice: Wind energy is most appropriate because offshore wind is nearly constant in coastal areas and is easy to transmit to the communities.

Identify `text(two)` examples of passive solar energy and `text(two)` examples of active solar energy.

The scientist claims that the landscape in the area changed over time. Which statement uses fossil evidence to `text(best)` support the scientist's claim?

A.Choice: The fossils show that the area had little to no water during the observed time.

B.Choice: The fossils show that the area remained covered in water during the observed time.

C.Choice: The fossils show that the area had little water at `text(first)` but became wetter during the observed time.

Content: Mass extinctions cause sudden reductions to biodiversity. Species loss can have a `text(negative)` effect on an ecosystem. Which statement `text(best)` describes how a mass extinction might have a beneficial effect on an ecosystem?

A.Choice: The change in the ecosystem increases the opportunities for diverse organisms to find mates and produce offspring.

B.Choice: The accumulation of nutrients within the ecosystem ensures that all surviving organisms have direct access to nutrients.

C.Choice: The removal of organisms reduces competition for resources and provides an opportunity for some surviving species to adapt.

D.Choice: The decrease in animal populations enables plants to become reestablished in areas where all plants were `text(once)` eliminated.

Content: Scientists have proposed that at one time in `text(Earth's)` history there was a supercontinent called Pangaea, as shown in the diagram.
problems/MS22G8S/media/5a.jpg
Which statement describes the causes that `text(most likely)` led to the breaking apart of Pangaea?

A.Choice: Solar radiation from the `text(Sun)` along with meteor impacts caused cracks to form in Pangaea.

B.Choice: Convection in `text(Earth's)` interior caused Pangaea to separate into several different landmasses.

C.Choice: Weathering and erosion caused earthquakes that resulted in breaks in the continental crust.

D.Choice: Forces from within `text(Earth)` resulted in some areas sinking below sea level and others rising upward.

Content: The diagram shows a geological cross section of rock layers at `text(Earth's)` surface.
problems/MS22G8S/media/6a.jpg
Which statement `text(best)` describes the pattern shown in the diagram?

A.Choice: The layers formed due to varying temperatures within `text(Earth's)` crust, and the shifting is due to `text(Earth's)` gravitational pull toward `text(Earth's)` core.

B.Choice: The layers formed due to varying temperatures within `text(Earth's)` crust, and the shifting is due to the movement of `text(two)` tectonic plates at a plate boundary.

C.Choice: The layers formed due to different types of sediment being deposited on `text(Earth's)` surface, and the shifting is due to `text(Earth's)` gravitational pull toward `text(Earth's)` core.

D.Choice: The layers formed due to different types of sediment being deposited on `text(Earth's)` surface, and the shifting is due to the movement of `text(two)` tectonic plates at a plate boundary.

Content: A student learned that the Himalayas were formed by the collision of the Indian Plate and the Eurasian Plate `50` `text(million years)` ago. The student gathered the following information.

:ibox:`bbtext(Data)`

• Scientists estimate that the elevation of the Himalayas has been increasing by over `9` `text(meters per century)` `(100` `text(years))`.
• In `text(1954)`, the elevation of the highest peak of the Himalayas, Mount Everest, was measured to be `8text(,)848` `text(meters)`.
• In `text(May 2019)`, Mount Everest was measured to be `8text(,)848.86` `text(meters)`.
Based on this information, which statement `text(best)` describes the elevation of the Himalayas?

A.Choice: The elevation of the Himalayas is increasing at a faster rate than in past `text(centuries)` because there are few acting causes of erosion at upper elevations.

B.Choice: The elevation of the Himalayas is increasing at a slower rate than in past `text(centuries)` because the causes of erosion increase their effect as the force of gravity decreases.

C.Choice: The elevation of the Himalayas is increasing at a faster rate than in past `text(centuries)` because the `text(two)` tectonic plates forming the range are colliding faster now than in the past.

D.Choice: The elevation of the Himalayas is increasing at a slower rate than in past `text(centuries)` because the pressure of the `text(two)` colliding tectonic plates is spread along a wider area now than in the past.

Content: Volcanic eruptions can be more easily predicted than earthquakes. Scientists constantly monitor certain factors to help make predictions about volcanic eruptions.
Which technological method of predicting volcanic eruptions is the `text(most)` effective?

A.Choice: Scientists use pH meters to measure the acidity of groundwater and surface water near volcanoes.

B.Choice: Scientists study the history of a volcano to determine when it was active and when it became dormant.

C.Choice: Scientists use satellite images to monitor changes in temperature and surface features of volcanoes in remote locations.

D.Choice: Scientists use seismographs to measure the length and strength of earthquakes to try to determine when a volcano will become active.

Content: Which statement `text(best)` describes the genetic material in the nucleus of pea plant cells?

Content: A student is reading about a bacterium that affects a host's digestive system. The bacterium undergoes a mutation that results in the production of a protein different from the `text(one)` originally coded for by the nucleus. The new protein provides the bacterium with a slime coating that is not affected by common antibiotics.
Which statement describes how this mutation `text(most likely)` affects the bacterium?

A.Choice:
The mutation is beneficial for the bacterium since it provides protection.
The mutation does not affect the host since mutated bacteria cannot reproduce.

B.Choice:
The mutation is not beneficial for the bacterium since it changes the genetic code of the bacterium.
The mutation does not affect the host since mutated bacteria cannot reproduce.

C.Choice:
The mutation is beneficial for the bacterium since it provides protection.
The mutation `text(negatively)` affects the host since the bacterium will be more likely to reproduce.

D.Choice:
The mutation is not beneficial for the bacterium since it changes the genetic code of the bacterium.
The mutation `text(negatively)` affects the host since the bacterium will be more likely to reproduce.

Content: Charles Darwin observed finches on the Galápagos Islands. Darwin noticed that finches on different islands had different beak shapes. He also noticed that there were many similarities shared by the finches from the different islands. These similarities convinced Darwin that the finches of the Galápagos Islands were all related through a common ancestor.
How did Charles Darwin explain the differences in the beak shapes of finches on the different islands?

A.Choice: The different beaks were needed to build a variety of bird nests on `text(each island)`.

B.Choice: The different beaks resulted from the different types of food available on `text(each island)`.

C.Choice: The different beaks provided protection from predators that were unique to `text(each island)`.

D.Choice: The different beaks were the result of unsuccessful mating among finches on `text(each island)`.

Content: A student is using an instrument to produce the following sound differences.

:ibox:`bbtext(Sound Differences)`

`1`. `text(one)` loud sound and `text(one)` quiet sound of the same pitch
`2`. `text(two)` sounds of different pitches
Which statement `text(best)` describes the sound differences produced by the student?

B.Choice: Both sound difference `1` and sound difference `2` are caused by the frequency of the sound waves.

D.Choice: Sound difference `1` is caused by the frequency of the sound waves, and sound difference `2` is caused by the amplitude of the sound waves.

Content: The electrical telegraph was the `text(first)` point-to-point messaging system. This system worked by sending electrical signals through a wire laid between `text(two)` stations. The telegraph system was eventually replaced by the telephone system.
Which statement `text(best)` identifies the primary difference between these `text(two)` communication systems?

A.Choice: The telegraph converts mechanical energy to electrical signals; the telephone converts sound energy to light waves that are reflected from satellites to receiving stations.

B.Choice: The telegraph converts sound waves to electrical signals that generate a code at the receiving station; the telephone converts light waves to electrical signals that generate sound waves.

C.Choice: The telegraph transmits mechanical signals to produce sound waves at the receiving station; the telephone produces sound waves that are converted to electrical energy at a receiving station.

D.Choice: The telegraph transmits coded electrical signals that are decoded at a receiving station; the telephone converts sound waves to electrical signals that travel through an electrical connection.
